result.title: Sampling Interventional Distributions with Orthogonal MMD Flow
result.summary: Many causal inference problems require sampling from interventional outcome distributions rather than estimating low-dimensional summaries. Existing approaches often rely on fitting generative models of the target distribution together with additional nuisance components, which can be computationally demanding for high-dimensional outcomes. We propose Interventional Maximum Mean Discrepancy Flow (IMMD-Flow), a particle-based method that instead represents the target interventional distribution through its kernel mean embedding. This kernel embedding admits a doubly robust, Neyman-orthogonal estimator with finite-sample guarantees and can be efficiently reused to sample from the interventional distribution via MMD gradient flow. IMMD-Flow accommodates both hard and soft interventions, admits theoretical guarantees for estimation and particle approximation, and extends to high-dimensional image outcomes through frozen encoders. Across image-based benchmarks, IMMD-Flow matches or improves upon state-of-the-art generative approaches while showing significant speed advantages.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 IMMD-Flow，用核均值嵌入直接表示干预后的结果分布，配合双稳健的 Neyman 正交估计和 MMD 梯度流做粒子采样，并借助冻结编码器扩展到图像结果，兼具有限样本与粒子近似保证。
